rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate all eight compounds and identify critical separations. The strong final solvent reduces the risk of missing late-eluting compounds, while the moderate temperature leaves room to explore temperature-dependent selectivity.

Keep the gradient fixed and raise temperature to test selectivity changes in the crowded middle cluster and late doublet. All compounds eluted quickly in the scouting run, so improving these critical separations takes priority over shortening the method.

Use a shallower gradient at the better-performing temperature to spread the critical pairs and test slope-dependent selectivity. The short elution window in injection 2 provides room to improve resolution while targeting a last peak below 10 minutes.

The shallower gradient resolves the early cluster but introduces a near-coelution later in the chromatogram. Lower temperature by one step to shift that pair’s selectivity while retaining the successful gradient slope and a likely sub-10-minute elution window.

Make the gradient slightly shallower to improve the sole unresolved pair at 55 C, where the other separations have useful margins. This tests whether full resolution can be reached near the 10-minute time threshold.

At 60 C, test a steeper gradient to move the late near-coeluting pair away from its crossover. Lowering the starting organic fraction may preserve separation in the early cluster while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Test a substantially shallower slope at 60 C to separate the late pair on the other side of its apparent selectivity crossover. A higher starting organic fraction should offset the longer gradient’s retention-time cost; the early cluster will be monitored for lost resolution.

Keep the higher starting organic fraction and make the gradient shallower to improve the early critical pair and probe the late pair’s crossover. Injection 7 leaves enough time margin that this longer gradient may still elute all peaks within 10 minutes.

Return to the best-performing region and steepen the gradient one step to move the late critical pair farther from coelution. This tests whether its resolution can reach 1.5 without losing too much of the early pair’s narrow resolution margin.

Test a gradient-to-hold transition: the shallower initial slope should improve the early critical pair, while the hold may separate the later pair differently from a continuing gradient. The final organic fraction is near the previously observed elution window, limiting—but not eliminating—the risk of excessive retention.

Test an intermediate slope at the higher starting organic fraction to shift the balance between the two critical separations. This may resolve the early pair without bringing the later pair too close to its crossover, while retaining ample time margin.

Use a slope of 0.045 organic fraction per minute, slightly steeper than injection 11, to improve the late critical pair while targeting at least 1.5 resolution for the early pair. The final organic fraction remains above the observed elution window, so all peaks should elute before the hold.

Injection 12 reaches the maximum CRF; now test a higher starting organic fraction to shorten elution while retaining full resolution. Keeping the endpoint and duration fixed also makes the slope shallower, which may offset some loss of early-pair separation.

Make the gradient one endpoint step shallower to recover the early separation lost in injection 13 while preserving some of its time advantage. Monitor the later critical pair, which may approach coelution as the slope decreases; injection 12 remains the maximum-score fallback.

Injection 12 already achieves the maximum score, but nearby high-temperature methods show a tight resolution tradeoff. Test low-temperature selectivity with a moderate gradient to look for a different route to full resolution and shorter elution.

Raise the starting organic fraction at 25 C to shorten retention and test whether the middle near-coelution responds favorably to the changed gradient window. Injection 12 remains the fully resolved, maximum-score reference.

Return to the maximum-score region and increase the slope slightly, from 0.045 to 0.04583 organic fraction per minute. This tests whether elution can be shortened while keeping the narrowly resolved early pairs at R ≥ 1.5; injection 12 remains the fallback.

The high-temperature method is near its resolution limit, so retain injection 12 as the best method and test a faster low-temperature alternative. A steeper gradient may move the middle pair away from its apparent crossover; the late pair will be checked for lost resolution.

Raise temperature one step in the fast low-temperature method to test whether selectivity improves both remaining critical pairs. Its 5.32-minute elution window offers a substantial speed advantage if full resolution can be recovered; injection 12 remains the maximum-score fallback.

Shorten the gradient one step to move the remaining middle near-coelution farther from its slope-dependent crossover. Check the neighboring separation carefully, since it has only modest margin; injection 12 remains the fully resolved maximum-score method.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction at 25 C can shift the middle critical pair while preserving the late separation and short elution time. Injection 12 remains the maximum-score method; this run seeks a faster fully resolved alternative.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step, following the improvement from injections 18 to 21. This may bring the late pair above R = 1.5 while further shortening elution; monitor the middle cluster for any loss of resolution.

Lengthen the gradient one step to improve both unresolved pairs in injection 22 while retaining its short elution window. The other middle-pair separation has enough margin to test this shallower slope; injection 12 remains the maximum-score fallback.

Raise temperature one step to test whether the newly fully resolved method can run faster without losing its critical middle separation. Injection 23 is now the fastest demonstrated maximum-score method and remains the fallback.

Test a higher starting organic fraction with a compensating shallower slope, seeking faster elution while preserving the critical middle separation. Injection 23 remains the fastest demonstrated fully resolved method, with the maximum CRF of 1.000.
